summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indologist and historian who studied at Deccan College, Elphinstone College, and Government Law College, Mumbai. He taught at the New English School (~1880–1885) and served as a mathematics teacher at Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

Bal Krishen Thapar was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at the University of the Punjab, under Mortimer Wheeler, and at Heidelberg. He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and Chairman of CCRT (1982–1992).
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indology scholar who held positions at Panjab University, serving as Assistant to Librarian (attested 1932) and in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1947).

Bangwei Wang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He earned his doctorate at Peking University (~1983–1987), where he became a Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies around 1993.

Banikanta Kakati worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He served as a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later as Dean and department head at Gauhati University (1948).

Bapudeva Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Sehore High School under Lancelot Wilkinson, as well as under Dhundiraja Misra and Sevarama. He taught at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (Sampurnanand Sanskrit University) from roughly 1841 to 1889.

Barbara E. Ward was a Sinologist who studied at Newnham College, the University of London, and LSE. She held posts at the University of Cambridge, Newnham College, Clare Hall, and visiting professorships at Cornell and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel, later holding research posts at the University of Berlin (2011–2015), Oxford, and the University of Vienna.

Barbara Mittler is a Sinologist and historian who studied at Pearson College, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and the University of Heidelberg. She held a post at the University of Heidelberg in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is an anthropologist in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Queen's University and completed her Ph.D. at SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran 1 in 2007.

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist who studied at Barnard College, Columbia, and Penn under W. Norman Brown, Stella Kramrisch, and Royal W. Weiler. She was a professor at Barnard College (1968–1993) and Columbia University (~1968–1993).

Barbra R. Clayton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her Ph.D. at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and held a position at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).

Barend Faddegon was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1893–1906) and subsequently served on the faculty there from 1907 to 1944, eventually becoming Emeritus Professor.

Barend J. ter Haar is a scholar of Sinology, history, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher and Susan Naquin, later holding posts at Heidelberg (~1994–2000) and as professor at Leiden (~2000–2013).

Barend Jan Terwiel is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Utrecht and the Australian National University. His academic posts included teaching at ANU, the University of Munich, and holding a chair at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).
Barnabé Brisson studied at the College of Juilly, École polytechnique, and École des Ponts ParisTech. He later held an academic post at École des Ponts ParisTech from 1820 to 1824.

Barry Kerzin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Southern California, later serving as an assistant professor at the University of Washington (1985–1989) and professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Barry Sautman specializes in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at UCLA, NYU, and Columbia University, and served as an assistant professor at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology from 1993 to 2008.
Bart Dessein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Willemen and has served as an Associate Professor at Ghent University (attested 2014–2019).

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn under Friedrich Ritschl, and Göttingen. He served as Professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and professor at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).
